events.credibility_reason: The paper's text is internally inconsistent about whether the parity constraint theorems are proved or only stated, and sorry status is unverified; in any case it formalizes known 1967 results.

events.ai_basis: The proof of Theorem 1 was produced by ChatGPT Astra.

why: The statement asks only whether an opposite-parity amicable pair exists. No event exhibits one or proves none exists. The shape constraints (Kanold's structure result, Gioia–Vaidya, D'Abramo, Yamada) are conditional on such a pair existing and settle nothing, so they are none. Lower bounds on the size or complexity of coprime opposite-parity pairs (Kanold, Hagis) were answered bound; this was a close call between bound and none, but they are pre-snapshot and cannot affect the status. Jaroma–Mitchell settles a restricted class (pairs with a Fibonacci or Lucas member), so it is a case, also pre-snapshot. The OEIS parity census is instances. Of the post-snapshot events, the 2026 Lean paper formalizes known constraints (none). Mavaddat–Alikhani does not address parity (none). Pollack's AI-generated density bound answers a different question about amicable numbers, the count A(x), not parity (variant). Its ai_role is generated on the author's own statement, but that credit does not attach to the parity question.
doubts: The pre-snapshot journal papers were known only through citations. Their verification is marked digested because they appeared in journals of record, and the exact hypotheses of the Hagis and Kanold bounds were not confirmed. None of this affects the post-snapshot reading.
